clue.text: Guy in Love Island is a horny bounder

indicators.note: the teasing word sits inside the zero and the island letter, as a guy might be inside a villa

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O
to guy someone is to mock them, as is to rib them

explanation.surface: A man on the reality show Love Island is called a randy leaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality TV dating show, which makes 'horny' look like a comment on a contestant.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope: it has horns and leaps, hence a horned bounder.

clue.text: Like a pub where all the hard liquor's been drunk down

definitions.text: Like a pub where all the hard liquor's been drunk
definitions.meaning: a bar with no spirits left is literally out of them
down means depressed, low in mood

explanation.surface: A dry pub after a long night, with only 'down' tacked on to finish the thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of spirits is an idiom for being dejected or low, which is what down means.

clue.text: Where birds are devouring corn seriously

indicators.note: the phrase for nesting birds swallows the grain word, putting it inside

parts.note: birds are in a nest, so in nest
an ear of corn is the grain-bearing head of the plant

explanation.surface: Nesting birds gobbling grain with great determination.
explanation.walkthrough: The birds' location is read as the two words 'in nest', which split open to take the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest means doing it sincerely, without joking: an adverbial idiom.

clue.text: Barring Connery's lead, classic version of Bond

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so one letter is kept out of the word for classic

parts.note: a classic is iconic, a standard everyone recognises

indicators.note: the lead of a name is its first letter

explanation.surface: A film buff's verdict: without Sean Connery, a definitive take on James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond, but it is the chemical bond.
explanation.definitionFit: An ionic bond is one kind of chemical bond, formed by electrostatic attraction between charged ions.

clue.text: Public figure giving hint

parts.note: overt means open, done in public view
one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A celebrity dropping a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a subtle suggestion or implication, so it is a hint.

clue.text: Tardily, woke Liberal goes on record, boring new voters

indicators.note: the combined piece drills into the rearranged electorate, sitting inside it
new suggests the letters of voters are made afresh in another order
in a down entry, going on something means sitting above it, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Political scene: a progressive Liberal makes a record that bores fresh voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woke' looks like the political adjective but is the past tense of wake. 'new' rearranges VOTERS to OVERST, and 'boring' puts LEP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to sleep past the time intended, so someone who overslept woke late.

clue.text: Fare pocketed in voyage at sea

indicators.note: the answer is tucked inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Food tucked away on board during an ocean crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' could be a ticket price on a voyage, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, and fare is the food provided at a meal.

clue.text: Abridge Old Testament book, suppressing hard term

parts.note: to abridge is to cut down, to trim

indicators.note: suppressing a letter means keeping it out of the book's name

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Old Testament
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An editor cutting a biblical book and censoring a tough word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' removes H from ESTHER, leaving ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is one of three academic periods in a year in some systems, so a term.

clue.text: Subtle, absorbing end of tale one's related

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so the final letter goes inside the word for subtle

parts.note: nice can mean subtle or fine, as in a nice distinction

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A refined storyteller, caught up in the ending, confides a family connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle' means NICE in its older sense of finely discriminating.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a brother's or sister's daughter, so she is one who is a relative.

clue.text: Stage direction stops working in theatre play

indicators.note: the direction plugs the gap in the rearranged letters, like a stopper
working suggests the letters are being worked into a new order

parts.note: enter is the classic stage direction for an actor coming on

explanation.surface: A stage cue halts the work going on in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' looks like part of the definition, but it is fodder; 'working' gives THETAINER and 'stops' plugs the cue into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entertainer is John Osborne's 1957 drama about a failing music-hall performer.

clue.text: Feature of Love's Labour's Lost nothing but repetition

parts.note: all can mean nothing but, as in all talk
iteration is the act of repeating

explanation.surface: A critic sniffs that Shakespeare's comedy is merely repetitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The title Love's Labour's Lost repeats the L sound at the start of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliteration repeats opening consonants across words, and the play's title is a famous example.

clue.text: Pro card player's inspired about project

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the player takes the short word inside

parts.note: East is one of the four players at bridge; the 's stands for has
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A professional bridge player has been inspired by something.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: To project figures is to estimate them for the future, which is to forecast.

clue.text: Happened by chance to ring, interrupted by heavy metal

indicators.note: the chiming word is broken into with the metal symbol placed inside

parts.note: a bell rings
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a heavy metal

explanation.surface: A phone ringing is drowned out by a blast of heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' sounds like the music genre but is iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell is the past tense of befall, meaning to happen, often to someone, as if by fate.

clue.text: Pastry crust of canapé, something consumed in bits

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

indicators.note: the crust of something is its outside, so the first and last letters

parts.note: a meal is something eaten

explanation.surface: Pastry topping on party nibbles, eaten bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done gradually, one part at a time, which is in bits.

clue.text: Rich man from South Africa confined, having been given a stretch?

parts.note: Elon Musk, the billionaire, was born in South Africa
gated is British school slang for confined to the premises as a punishment

explanation.surface: A wealthy South African is locked up and given a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stretch' is slang for a prison sentence, but here it means being lengthened. Being gated is a British school punishment of being kept in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elongated has been lengthened, literally given a stretch; the question mark flags the wordplay on prison time.

clue.text: English following type of stock car

indicators.note: in a down entry, following means coming after, so the English letter goes last

parts.note: Limousin is a breed of beef cattle, i.e. livestock

explanation.surface: A stock car racer behind an English rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock car' looks like one phrase, but 'stock' means livestock and 'car' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large, luxurious car, often chauffeur-driven.

clue.text: Traditional motifs in piece of music caught by solver in France

indicators.note: the musical work is held inside the French pronoun

parts.note: the solver is you, which in French is toi
op. is short for opus, a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: Recurring themes in a tune that a puzzler hears while holidaying in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Topoi is the plural of topos, a stock theme or convention in literature or rhetoric.

clue.text: Post mountain-climbing setter in building

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
cement is the building material that sets

explanation.surface: A setter takes a mountaineering job inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' would usually be the crossword compiler, ME, but here it is a substance that sets. 'climbing' reverses ALP to PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement is a job or position, which is what a post is.

clue.text: Comparative magnitude of bits east of desert

indicators.note: in an across entry, east of means to the right, so after

parts.note: to rat is to desert, as on one's friends
binary digits, 1 and 0, look like I and O

explanation.surface: Fragments found to the east of a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, so comparative magnitude.

clue.text: Less wild path for conquering warrior

parts.note: tamer means less wild
a lane is a path or narrow road

explanation.surface: A gentler route chosen by an invading soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamerlane, or Timur, was the 14th-century Turco-Mongol conqueror of much of Asia.

clue.text: Hollow area poor driver ends up in — he leaves it

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the pronoun is taken out of the phrase

parts.words: area poor driver ends up in
parts.note: in golf, a poor drive lands in the rough, the long grass off the fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer's bad drive finds a dip, and he walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golf club. 'leaves' takes HE out of THE ROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long narrow depression, so a hollow.

clue.text: Amerindian's poetic apostrophe to a wise man

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is just the person

parts.note: an apostrophe is a speech addressing someone, opened poetically with O
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A Native American is addressing a wise man in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apostrophe' looks like the punctuation mark but is the rhetorical address.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains, now based in Oklahoma.

clue.text: Summons a vehicle back across open ground

indicators.note: the reversed pair stretches across the rearranged word, holding it inside
back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: ground, as in milled, means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vehicle reversing across a stretch of open land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open ground' reads as a field, but 'ground' means milled: it gives POEN, held within SUBA from 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a writ ordering someone to attend court: a legal summons.

clue.text: It's said to dismiss Poland's No 1 playmaker

indicators.note: number one means the first letter of the word

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was a maker of plays, a playwright

explanation.surface: A sports commentator calls for Poland's star midfielder to be sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playmaker' suggests a football midfielder but means a writer of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an exclamation of contempt or impatience, uttered to wave something away.

clue.text: Rolls topped with unwrapped spam or fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, topped with means the other piece sits above
unwrapped means the outer letters are stripped off

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce, often just called a Rolls

explanation.surface: A lunch choice: bread rolls with tinned meat or fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like bread rolls but stands for the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon in its freshwater stage, so a fish.

clue.text: Poet, reading the Iliad, mostly stunned

indicators.note: stunned suggests the letters are knocked senseless and fall into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A poet left speechless while reading Homer's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts Iliad to ILIA; 'stunned' rearranges READING THE ILIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri was the Florentine poet who wrote the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Imported copper: high grade, half mended

indicators.note: high, as in intoxicated, suggests the letters are reeling into a new order
half means the first three of the six letters

explanation.surface: A metal shipment of top quality that has been half repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal but is a police officer; 'high' looks like part of 'high grade'. 'high' rearranges GRADE plus MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer; copper is slang for police officer, and the word is borrowed from French.

clue.text: Deity in religious books with pale covering

indicators.note: the colourless word wraps around the scriptures, holding them inside

parts.note: wan means pale
OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: A god appearing in scripture wrapped in a pale cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Wotan is the German name for Odin, chief god in Norse and Germanic mythology.
